findings.description: P1 imports every shell export into repository-selected Quality commands while keeping API-key stripping Agent-only, newly exposing shell-only credentials despite describing a toolchain environment.
findings.recommendation: Define, test, and document a Quality-safe shell overlay that preserves PATH and toolchain discovery plus override precedence while excluding direct provider keys and other credential classes.

result.summary: Revise the plan to keep Quality tool discovery without exposing shell-only credentials to repository-selected commands.

checklist.description: Extend the central effective launch-environment policy with a Quality-specific shell projection that overlays only PATH and explicitly vetted non-secret tool-discovery variables between the inherited daemon environment and process-specific overrides, falls back non-disruptively when shell capture fails, and leaves Agent-only credential handling and unrelated process owners unchanged.

Add focused environment-policy and supervised Quality-command regression coverage showing that a synthetic shell-only tool path reaches the executed command, explicit allowed-variable overrides retain precedence, and direct provider keys plus representative non-provider credentials exported by the shell are not imported.

Update the affected process intent documentation to describe Quality's allowlisted host-shell tool-discovery contract, its exclusion of arbitrary exports and credentials, the absence of a hardcoded dotnet path, and the need to restart the daemon after shell configuration changes.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The revised plan replaces the unrestricted shell import with an allowlist-only Quality projection, adds regression coverage that shell-exported provider and non-provider credentials remain absent while PATH-based tool discovery and override precedence work, and documents that security boundary.

result.summary: Give daemon-launched Quality commands access to shell-configured toolchains through a narrowly allowlisted host-shell overlay so tools such as dotnet are discoverable without exposing shell-only credentials to repository-selected commands.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan can be executed without violating the constitution, governance rules, or enabled guidance.

checklist.evidence: EffectiveLaunchEnvironment now overlays the cached host-shell environment for ProcessOwner::Quality only when a key is in the explicit PATH, PATHEXT, DOTNET_ROOT, DOTNET_ROOT_X64, or DOTNET_ROOT_X86 allowlist. The projection is applied after inherited daemon values and before process overrides; an empty or failed shell capture leaves inherited and explicit values intact. Non-Agent/Quality owners avoid shell capture, and the existing Agent full-shell overlay plus final direct-provider-key removal remains unchanged.

Added launch-policy tests proving allowlist filtering, PATH and DOTNET_ROOT override precedence, inherited-value retention, and empty-capture fallback. Added a supervised Quality child-process regression whose executable exists only on the synthetic shell PATH and which observes DOTNET_ROOT while OPENAI_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL shell exports remain unset.

Updated docs/intent/04-infrastructure/01-process.md to define Quality's exact tool-discovery allowlist, credential and arbitrary-export exclusion, inherited/override precedence, capture fallback, absence of a hardcoded dotnet installation path, and daemon restart requirement after shell configuration changes.
